focus: The commit and push path: which local hook checks run, what each costs, and whether hook time explains the operator wait
noveltyJustification: 4 of 5 findings were fully new (hook gate inventory, measured checker costs, pre-push test removal, missing test entrypoint) and 1 was partially new (hook cost versus CI cost framing).
keyQuestions: Which pre-commit and pre-push hook checks cost the most wall-clock time, and which could move to CI or run only on changed paths?
answeredQuestions: Which pre-commit and pre-push hook checks cost the most wall-clock time, and which could move to CI or run only on changed paths?
ruledOut: Running a real commit to time the hook end to end
Reporting the pre-commit gates as bloat without measurement
Adding a package.json scripts block as a recommendation

graphEvents.label: Which hook checks cost the most wall-clock time
Local hook path measures about 1s commit and 3s push

label: pre-commit is 1056 lines running 13 named blocking gates
Every measured local checker finishes at or under 0.13s (comment hygiene 0.09s, phrase lint 0.09s, agent mirror sync 0.13s, route guard 0.09s, doc version 0.09s, contract drift 0.09s)
Commit-hook cost is process startup: at least twelve node spawns at 0.03-0.13s each, about one second total
pre-push runs no test suite; its own comment records that report-only suites moved to CI
Track-root sweep is the costliest local check at 2.27s, pre-push only, once per pushed ref
No root package.json and no scripts block in .skilled/package.json, so no aggregate local test command exists
Hook time cannot explain a multi-minute wait: commit about 1s, push about 3s, versus 10s cheapest and 595s most expensive CI workflow
Only CI workflow time can yield minute-scale savings; hook cuts are second-scale

direction: Timing the hook by making a real commit
reason: A commit writes the index and object store outside the lineage write surface
